key_insight: Vision-Language-Action models often ignore language instructions and default to visually frequent behaviors; this paper identifies and quantifies these "counterfactual failures" and shows how targeted evaluation and interventions can reduce vision-overrides-language errors.
problem_solved: Addresses the failure mode where VLAs follow dataset-induced visual shortcuts (frequently seen objects or actions) instead of the actual language intent, causing incorrect or unsafe robot behaviors when scene-specific language supervision is weak.
method: Define and systematically evaluate "counterfactual failures" in VLAs with controlled scenario perturbations that separate language intent from visual priors.
Introduce diagnostic metrics to quantify how often models ignore language and favor visually frequent choices.

Propose mitigation strategies such as counterfactual data augmentations, language-anchoring objectives, and bias-aware training (e.g., reweighting or contrastive examples) to encourage language-faithful actions.
impact: Helps researchers and practitioners detect when embodied agents rely on visual shortcuts and provides practical evaluation and training recipes to make VLAs more reliable and aligned with language instructions—critical for safe, generalizable robot behavior.
visual_elements: Side-by-side scenario diagram showing (A) instruction + scene where vision wins (wrong object/action) and (B) same instruction with corrected, language-faithful behavior after mitigation.
Bar chart comparing counterfactual failure rates across baseline VLA, diagnostic metric scores, and after proposed mitigation.
Attention / saliency overlays on scene images illustrating when the model attends to irrelevant frequent objects vs. the language-relevant target.
Flowchart of the evaluation + mitigation pipeline: perturb scenes → measure failures → apply augmentation/reweighting → re-evaluate.
paper_title: When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs
paper_authors: Yu Fang, Yuchun Feng, Dong Jing, Jiaqi Liu, Yue Yang
